Build custom database object for use with phylotypr

Source: R/create_database.R
create_database.Rd

The create_database() function builds a classification_database object that can be used to generate the kmer database for downstream use in classify_sequences(). This function is only necessary if you are building your own database or modifying one of the existing databases provided in {phylotypr} or {phylotyprrefdata}.

Usage

create_database(sequence_name, sequence, taxonomy, reference_data = NULL)

Arguments

sequence_name

A character vector of identifiers for each sequence in the database. Should have the same number of values as found in the sequence and taxonomy vectors.

sequence

A character vector of the sequences that are included in the database. Should have the same number of values as found in the sequence_name and taxonomy vectors.

taxonomy

A character vector of taxonomy data for each sequence in the database. Should have the same number of values as found in the sequence_name and sequence vectors. The format of each value should be with each taxonomic level separated by a semicolon. Ideally each value in taxonomy will have the same number of levels.

reference_data

single row data frame object that has columns vendor, name, version, usage, notes, method_url, documentation_url, and citation. This is supplied with databases obtained from phylotyprrefdata. This information is only used if user supplied sequences are supplied as a strollur object.

Value

A classification_database object, which is a list containing the fields seq_taxonomy_data and reference_data. These are both data.frame objects.

Examples

sequence_name <- c("seq_a", "seq_b", "seq_c")
sequence <- c("AAAATCGAGTA", "ATGCGCTCCCC", "ATGCGCTCCCC")
genera <- c("A;b;C;d", "A;b;C;e", "A;b;C;e")

create_database(
  sequence_name = sequence_name,
  sequence = sequence,
  taxonomy = genera
)
#> $seq_taxonomy_data
#>   sequence_name    sequence taxonomy.1 taxonomy.2 taxonomy.3 taxonomy.4
#> 1         seq_a AAAATCGAGTA          A          b          C          d
#> 2         seq_b ATGCGCTCCCC          A          b          C          e
#> 3         seq_c ATGCGCTCCCC          A          b          C          e
#> 
#> $reference_data
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "classification_database"
